# UntrustedShellCommand

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Security](/rules/#security)

Detect request-derived data reaching a shell-command sink in syntax-capable position without proven appropriate argument escaping or strict validation.

## Example

```php{2,3,4}
<?php
system('viewer ' . $_GET['path']);
$listing = `ls {$_GET['dir']}`;
proc_open('convert ' . $_GET['file'], [], $pipes);

// Not reported: the request only selects a constant, or contributes a number.
$mode = match ($_GET['mode']) { 'full' => '--full', default => '--quick' };
system('backup ' . $mode);
system('head -c ' . strlen($_POST['body']) . ' /dev/zero');
proc_open(['convert', $_GET['file']], [], $pipes);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Keep untrusted input out of shell command syntax.</li>
<li>line 3: Keep untrusted input out of shell command syntax.</li>
<li>line 4: Keep untrusted input out of shell command syntax.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Report request-derived data reaching a shell-command sink in syntax-capable position without proven appropriate argument escaping or strict validation.
- Shell-command sinks are the first (`command`) argument of resolved builtin `system`, `exec`, `shell_exec`, `passthru`, `popen` and `proc_open`, and the text of a backtick command expression, which PHP runs exactly like `shell_exec`. A call to a project function is a sink when its summary forwards an argument, or request data it reads itself, to one of these sinks: `proc_open` and a backtick command count there like the other four, except a `proc_open` the function gives an argument vector (E1).
- Decide per operand whether request data can become command text. Concatenation, interpolation and `??` carry any of their operands; a conditional or `match` expression carries only its result operands, never its condition or subject; a variable with a single reaching assignment carries what that assignment carries. Every other request-derived operand carries its data unless E1 or E3 applies. A variable is followed to its reaching assignment only when its scope cannot rebind it behind that assignment; a reference alias, a by-reference closure capture, `foreach` or argument, a `catch` binding or `static` declaration of the same name, `extract()`, an assignment through a variable variable, a `global` declaration of it or a `$GLOBALS` access that is not a different literal entry keeps the report.
- Resolve builtin calls and named arguments before checking the contract. Project-local callees are considered only when their bodies or immutable summaries establish the required facts. The default is enabled, with positive proof required.
- For flow-dependent conditions, require a reachable source-to-use path with no intervening invalidation. Unknown calls, ambiguous aliases, recursion or analysis-budget exhaustion cannot establish definite facts.

Project method wrappers are followed only when a single visible declaration is fixed by a final receiver class, a final method, or a private method accessible at the call. Open overridable methods, ambiguous declarations, conditional class bodies and trait bodies do not establish a wrapper sink. Static calls must name a static method. These contracts compose through nested project wrappers and refresh when class or method dispatch metadata changes.

A wrapper dependency that reads only array values preserves the numeric safety of an array whose values are all numbers, booleans or null. Array keys, whole-array formatting and mixed key/value dependencies remain untrusted; numeric conversion of extracted keys can establish safety again. Return and reference-output dependencies preserve the same distinction.

## Exceptions (no report)

- E1. Resolved argument-vector execution, escaped arguments with validated option policy, constant commands and unknown flows are excluded. `proc_open` whose command is an array literal, a variable holding one or an array-typed expression is argument-vector execution. A command assembled only from constants selected by request data (for example `match` arms or conditional branches that are all literals) is a constant command.
- Unresolved targets, incomplete required facts, suppressed findings and PHP versions lacking the referenced API or language feature produce no report. User declarations shadowing builtin names are not builtin contracts.

- E3. Known boolean or numeric scalar output and resolved builtin `md5`, `sha1`, `hash` or `hash_hmac` hexadecimal output cannot inject the target text syntax. Raw binary or unknown output modes retain source taint. These narrow text proofs do not establish URL or filesystem-path authorization.
- E4. Under E3, numeric scalar output covers: integer, float and boolean casts; the results of `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` and `**` and of unary `+` and `-`, which yield a number or fail; a resolved builtin call whose declared result on the configured PHP version consists only of integer, float, boolean and null (such as `strlen`, `count` or `strpos`); and `+` when at least one operand is a literal or such a builtin call. `+` between two operands that may both be arrays is an array union that keeps request-derived elements and is not excluded. Bitwise operators on strings produce strings and are not excluded.
- A wrapper call is not reported when every request-derived argument written at the call is excluded by E1, E3 or E4.
- Request data that a `switch` compared with constant labels is the matched label inside an arm reached only through string labels that do not read as numbers (not empty and not starting, after whitespace, with a digit, a sign or a dot), and after the switch when every other way out replaced it or left the scope: `switch ($sort) { case 'name': case 'date': break; default: $sort = 'name'; }` validates `$sort`. A numeric, empty, boolean or null label, a label expression, a fall-through from another arm, a `default` arm and any other subject prove nothing. The subject is a plain variable or an element of a request superglobal read under one constant key (`switch ($_GET['action'])`, not `$_FILES`); the element is the matched label only while nothing that may run code is evaluated: a call, an object creation, an assignment, an `unset`, or the use of a local variable, property, offset of a local or class constant ends it, as does a reference to the superglobal. A `switch (true)` reads each case expression like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain.

## Fix

No automatic fix: executable, option boundaries and allowed arguments require explicit policy.

## PHP versions

Apply only on PHP versions supporting the referenced APIs and syntax (within PHP 5.3–8.5). Builtin behavior and argument contracts follow the configured PHP version. Extension-specific calls require resolved extension API symbols; do not treat same-named application functions as extension calls.

## Options

None. Enable or disable this rule through normal rule configuration.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "UntrustedShellCommand": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore UntrustedShellCommand
```
